description: Jordaan cornice houses (lijstgevels) of the 18th-19th c. and their 1880-1910 rebuilds (Bloemgracht, Rozengracht, Westerstraat): 4.5-8 m fronts of red-brown brick, a ground storey and two to four upper storeys of about 2.8 m; three axes (two under 4.6 m, four over 7.6 m) of white T-windows with white sills; a plain white cornice, sometimes one small dormer over the middle

match.note: Bloemgracht 80-128 and 138-300 (2024-12 strips): cornices at 10.7, 13.5 and 14.5 m over three to five storeys; a front whose skyline reads a tall crown is the gable house's (crownMatch)

dormer.note: Bloemgracht 80-128 (169914): one small white dormer over the middle

door-left.note: house door on the left axis; a pand whose door reads on the right is mirrored (mirrorForDoor), so a two-axis front keeps a valid door bay

rhythm.groundFloor: a house door and windows, or a shop
rhythm.roofline: a plain white cornice, sometimes one dormer
schemaLimits: the 18th c. cornice ornament (Louis XIV/XV) is drawn as a plain cornice

evidence.citation: strip.jpg 2024-12 at 0.42x with a metre grid: ground to 3.6 m; storeys of 2.8-2.9 m; cornices at 14.5 m (with a dormer to 16 m) and 10.7 m
